I had a regular manicure done here end of September. The technician arrived late to the appointment. She used an electric file on my cuticles and ruined my nails, causing what is called " Rings of fire" due to over-filing the nail plate, which creates damage and sensitivity. It has now been 6 weeks since my appointment and my nails are still in very bad shape. It can take 4 to 6 months for a fingernail to fully grow out and possibly up to 9 months for the nail to look completely normal again !!  The manicure cost me $40 and absolutely ruined my nails. My nails keep breaking and i have to keep them super short until the ring of fire completely grows out.  The workers were all rushed and most of them arrived late and several clients were waiting. So very unprofessional nail spot and they will cause serious nail damage. Never let a technician use an electric file on your cuticles.

I never leave reviews but this experience was super disappointing and expensive. I’ve gotten two hard gel sets done here. The first one was so beautifully done, my cuticles looked great, french was perfect. Only issue is the set broke and chipped very quickly. I was back with multiple broken nails in a little over 2 weeks. Hard gel has always lasted 4 weeks for me with no chipping, just the need for a fill. I went back to give them another chance because I did love the manicure and thought it was a fluke. I asked to see the same girl but they put me with a different one who commented on how thin the set was and said she had to redo all of it, no fill possible. This one lasted less than a week before chipping began and the top coat was coming off on the tips of every nail. Within a few more days, three were broken. I had a super busy schedule so I wasn’t able to deal with nails or come in until the two week mark (my fault). I called and let them know what happened, they said they’d fix it. I came in at my appointment time but she had no idea I was scheduled and had me wait 20 minutes before looking at my nails and telling me she’d charge me for a fix after saying on the phone they’d take care of it. This took a total of an hour out of the work day to get to and from the salon…just to leave with nothing done. Wish they were more organized, considerate with their customers, and had better quality products that lasted longer on clients. It’s a great location and they take their time on the manicures. Sad.

I received a Lash Lift & Tint and Brow Wax & Tint from Sinthia in June 2026. I am so happy with the results!  The experience was so relaxing from the minute I arrived. The shop is set up to be calming and it’s clear that there was lots of thought put into every detail of the atmosphere and client experience.  Sinthia took the time to ask about my lash and brow preferences, even guiding me through the best color choices to match my natural hair color, and explaining different styles of lashes and brow shapes. I would have chosen a color much too dark for my brows if she had not helped me choose something that matched better. I always appreciate when beauty professionals are willing to kindly redirect toward a better idea and make sense of why. It was neat that she was able to customize how the tint was used on my brow hairs versus the skin. I had no idea that was even a distinction to make. When it came to aftercare instructions, Sinthia answered all of my questions and gave helpful, detailed examples that I had not heard before from prior estheticians. She was so sweet, knowledgeable, and had such positive, calm, kind energy all throughout my visit.  The results of my services were gorgeous and I’ve felt so pretty with my brows and lashes ever since. It’s been so great to not need to worry about makeup during the summer - so grateful the results have lasted beautifully for almost 6 weeks now.  I loved my appointment at Enchanted Beauty Bar and will be returning soon.

I made an appointment with Amber (hair Braider) over 30 days prior for Thursday, June 23rd 2020. Amber has a policy where you have to pay a portion of your services to lock your appointment. Cool, I don’t mind and as a licensed cosmetologist myself, I understand that deposits are needed for better scheduling for everyone. I ask Amber would she prefer I pay in full, she says that’s fine and that’s when I send over my full payment.  Fast forward 30 days and it’s now June, 23rd. 3 hours before my appointment , Amber text’s me and asks me to come another time because her cousin is in town to visit (Okay...but you have work so I don’t understand why her cousin can’t wait?). She begs and pleads and she asks if I can come on Saturday instead at 2pm. I don’t really have a choice so I agree.  Saturday, 25th is here and I’ve arrived at the salon. 2:05 comes and she’s not here, 2:10 comes and she’s not here. I’m calling Amber and it’s going to voicemail and I’m texting her with no responses. I decide to call the owner Felicia (I’m not too for sure if that’s her name or not). I’m very angry at this point and I’m explaining to the owner that I was rescheduled for the sake of hang outs, I’ve been waiting for 30 mins for my now new appointment and I haven’t heard from her, etc etc. She tells me she will call me back. Amber then FINALLY gets ahold of me and tells me she won’t be able to arrive at the salon until 5pm because she’s stuck in traffic. She then asks me “did you call my boss?” I told her, of course I did. You rescheduled me once for the sake of hanging out, you can’t even show up on a new appointment time that YOU gave to me, and NOW you’re saying it’s going to have to be an additional 3 hour wait!? I live an hour away! If I can show up on time and schedule for you, you should do the same for  your clients. She then tells me she doesn’t like being talked to like a child (go figure) and she doesn’t like my “energy” so she won’t be servicing me at all and hangs up. The boss ends up texting me, and refunds me her self.  This place is a joke, from the owner to the staff. We’re not going to discuss how the other stylists working were wearing pajama pants, and another one wearing club wear with her Panties flowing over to make sure they are more than noticed. This is the stereotype of black owned businesses that unfortunately people believe in. As a black cosmetologist and business owner this is not only disappointing from a customers perspective, it’s heart breaking as a black business owner that this is what I have to fight towards proving I’m not and this is not a representation of us all.
